key_insight: Small emulated quantum circuit blocks can match or outperform a parameter-matched CNN in some medical-image regimes, but neither approach is universally best.
engineering_relevance: Hybrid quantum-inspired layers may be useful as drop-in alternatives in resource-constrained or medium-data settings, while classical CNNs remain stronger at larger scale.
method: Compared a Hybrid Quantum-inspired CNN (HQiCNN) against a parameter-matched classical CNN differing only by one intermediate dense layer.
Evaluated both models on two real medical image datasets across systematically varied hyperparameters and training-set sizes.
Added SHAP-based explainability metrics to compare where each model focuses in the image.
evidence_signal: Across fair, dataset- and hyperparameter-independent benchmarks, HQiCNN performed best in intermediate-data regimes, while the classical CNN achieved the top accuracies with the largest training sets; both models highlighted anatomically plausible regions.
watch_item: Quantum simulation scalability remains a concern, and entanglement may be unnecessary if similar performance can be achieved without it.
paper_title: Do emulated quantum circuits change what CNNs look at? Performance and explainability comparison in medical image classification
